decisions.evidence: Maker R1: “Add bookmarks with URL”; Client R1 asks to verify “a brand-new one and it sticking around”; Maker R2–R3 presents the seventh saved bookmark; Client R3 confirms “saving a fresh link… and having it stick around… work.”
decisions.note: Conforming save-by-URL decision. The clarification and temporary evidence dispute were resolved by the later live-app presentation, so they are linked rather than counted separately.

decisions.evidence: Client R1 asks whether the app will “pull in the page’s title”; Maker R2 calls the flow complete but specifies only “page title and description automatically”; Maker R3 again specifies only title and description. Client R3 accepts those two fields but never mentions the required favicon or preview image.
decisions.note: The final presented metadata scope omits favicon and preview image. The client expressed and verified title/description extraction but did not surface the remaining difference, so the divergence was unexpressed at implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Maker R2: “You can edit the fetched details before saving.” Client R2 calls this “exactly the flow I wanted to see,” while requesting better evidence of the save demonstration.
decisions.note: The recorded before-save editing decision conforms. No distinct decision about after-save editing was presented, so absent coverage is not converted into a divergence.

decisions.evidence: Maker R1: “Add bookmarks with… tags.” Client R1 observes tags in the library and says the organization side is covered well.
decisions.note: The presented tag-assignment behavior conforms at the prototype-review stage.

decisions.evidence: Maker R1 presents “Search with ⌘/Ctrl + K.” Client R1 and R3 acknowledge the search UI/function generally, but neither the presentation nor responses identify which bookmark fields are searched.
decisions.note: A search decision is recorded, but evidence cannot establish whether it performs the required full-text search over title, description, note, and URL. Final approval does not resolve those semantics.

decisions.evidence: Maker R1: “Grid/list views and sorting.” Client R1 sees “sorting,” and Client R3 includes it among the accepted management features.
decisions.note: The recorded ability to sort the bookmark list conforms; the particular UI and additional grid/list preference are orthogonal.

decisions.evidence: Maker R1 presents bookmarks with “notes.” No maker entry specifies Markdown authoring or rendered-note viewing, and the client never addresses note formatting or rendering.
decisions.note: Evidence establishes a note field but cannot determine whether the Markdown behavior required by the reference is present or divergent.

decisions.evidence: Maker R1: “Archive and restore functionality.” Client R3 expressly includes “archive” among the accepted management features.
decisions.note: Archiving with restoration is a conforming reversible archive decision. No contrary delete semantics were presented.

decisions.evidence: Maker R1 presents a “polished” manager with “Grid/list views.” Client R1 describes the library as “clean and easy to scan” and reports titles, descriptions, and tags, but the maker’s textual presentation does not establish whether every item exposes a favicon.
decisions.note: The readability-first portion appears consistent, but the evidence cannot independently establish full conformity or divergence for all required per-item fields; the final general approval does not resolve the favicon question.
